models_evaluated: PharmaAgent (LLM-based agentic system, high- and low-autonomy configurations)

links.outcome: Safety concerns in out-of-tolerance AI vancomycin dosing recommendations
links.effect: MAPE 21.8% high vs 37.8% low autonomy; within 25% of order in 73.4% vs 50.9%; 65.8% of 196 out-of-tolerance recommendations had a safety concern, more with low autonomy (OR 2.37)
links.quote: Pharmacist review of 196 out-of-tolerance recommendations found a safety concern in 65.8%, more often with low autonomy (odds ratio 2.37).

links.outcome: Silent deployment on live data revealing readiness of agentic dosing
links.effect: Two-month silent deployment across 403 dosing events identified performance below pharmacist benchmark (90.2% within 25%); neither configuration ready without pharmacist oversight
links.quote: A higher-autonomy agent that self-debugged its steps proved more robust than stricter engineering, but neither configuration is ready to dose patients without pharmacist oversight.

unlisted_practices: Comparing high-autonomy self-debugging agent design versus low-autonomy strictly engineered agent workflow
Providing institutional dosing guidelines to the agent versus not

links.outcome: Dosing agreement with the treating pharmacist compared with a second pharmacist
links.effect: Recommendations were within 25% of the treating pharmacist's order in 73.4% of high-autonomy and 50.9% of low-autonomy events, versus 90.2% for a second pharmacist.
links.quote: Across 403 dosing events in 316 patients, mean absolute percentage error against the treating pharmacist's order was 21.8% with high autonomy versus 37.8% with low autonomy, and recommendations were within 25% of the order in 73.4% versus 50.9% of events (P < 0.001); a second pharmacist was within 25% of the treating pharmacist's order in 90.2% of events.

links.outcome: Safety concerns in out-of-tolerance vancomycin dosing recommendations
links.effect: Safety concerns occurred in 65.8% of 196 out-of-tolerance recommendations and were more frequent with low autonomy (odds ratio 2.37).
links.quote: Pharmacist review of 196 out-of-tolerance recommendations found a safety concern in 65.8%, more often with low autonomy (odds ratio 2.37).

unlisted_practices: Higher agent autonomy with self-debugging versus lower autonomy with stricter engineering.

links.outcome: mean absolute percentage error against pharmacist order
links.effect: MAPE was 21.8% for high autonomy and 37.8% for low autonomy compared to the treating pharmacist's order.
links.quote: Across 403 dosing events in 316 patients, mean absolute percentage error against the treating pharmacist's order was 21.8% with high autonomy versus 37.8% with low autonomy, and recommendations were within 25% of the order in 73.4% versus 50.9% of events (P < 0.001); a second pharmacist was within 25% of the treating pharmacist's order in 90.2% of events.

links.effect: Neither the high- nor low-autonomy configuration was deemed ready to dose patients without oversight.
links.quote: A higher-autonomy agent that self-debugged its steps proved more robust than stricter engineering, but neither configuration is ready to dose patients without pharmacist oversight.
